QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_19

question.text: The High-Water Mark (HWM) of a Category III AIF is:

answer.text: The highest NAV (net of operating expenses, transaction expenses and management fees) achieved by the fund at year-end
The peak GNAV during any hour
The initial subscription price plus GST

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines the High-Water Mark as the highest NAV — net of operating expenses, transaction expenses, and management fees — achieved by the Category III AIF at year-end. HWM is used together with the hurdle rate to determine the base for computing incentive fees. The Trap: Highest leverage, a peak intra-day GNAV, and the initial subscription price plus GST are not the workbook's HWM definition. Note: The HWM definition is taken from the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook (Series XIX-B).
